verdict_reasoning: No objection survived at level 1: message #1 shows a hash join of about 1739 ms chosen over a 2.7 ms parameterized nested loop because a path was lost. Two fixable design points remain. maintenance-fit-1 applies only to the add_path() patch, which message #2 already moves away from. maintenance-fit-2 asks for the contract of the new FDW callback, and message #3 supports that design.

brief.title: Keep parameterized foreign paths so append can use parameterized nested loop
brief.problem: add_path() can discard a parameterized foreign scan path when its cost and row count tie with a non-parameterized one. If one partition loses its parameterized path, the planner cannot build a parameterized Append, so it picks a hash join over a cheaper parameterized nested loop. This hits partitioned tables with postgres_fdw partitions and use_remote_estimate on.
brief.proposed_design: Patch 0001 (Pyhalov, WIP) changes add_path() in pathnode.c to keep all differently parameterized paths. The alternative (Kashkin) keeps add_path() as is and adds an FDW callback so reparameterize_path() can rebuild a parameterized foreign scan path when needed. An optional postgres_fdw patch caches parameterized path cost estimates to avoid repeat remote EXPLAIN round trips.
user_visible_surface: New FDW API callback to reparameterize foreign scan paths, called from reparameterize_path() (alternative design).
postgres_fdw implements the new callback and caches remote cost estimates for parameterized paths (optional patch).
Plan choice changes: queries may get a parameterized nested loop where they got a hash join before.
author_claims: In the example, the hash join takes about 1739 ms and the parameterized nested loop plan takes about 2.7 ms.
The planner chose the hash join because a parameterized path was missing, not because of cost.
Reparameterization fits the current path dominance model and builds extra foreign paths only when needed.
The cache avoids repeated remote EXPLAIN calls for paths already costed and rejected.
brief.thread_state: Etsuro Fujita gave +1 to the reparameterization approach and pointed to his own similar FDW API proposal from the foreign-table-inheritance work. Nobody has answered him, and nobody has reviewed the first patch.
unclear: The material does not say which of the two designs the authors plan to pursue.
The name, signature and documentation of the new FDW callback are not shown.
No planning-time or memory numbers are given for keeping all parameterized paths.
The proposal does not say how the cache is keyed or when it is invalidated.
No comparison with Fujita's earlier FDW API proposal is given.

prior_attempts.title: A hook for path-removal decision on add_path
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P2 proposed an extension hook to decide path removal in add_path(). Patch 0001 changes the dominance rule in core, and the alternative design leaves add_path() alone and reparameterizes foreign paths through a new FDW callback.

objections.title: Keeping all parameterized paths in add_path() costs every query
objections.failure_scenario: A user runs a 10-way join on local tables with many indexes and no foreign tables. Every base and join rel now keeps every differently parameterized path, so pathlists grow and join search does more work. The user sees higher planning time and memory after upgrade, with no plan change.
objections.argument: Patch 0001 changes add_path() in pathnode.c, which every rel of every query goes through. The problem shown in message #1 is specific to postgres_fdw partitions with use_remote_estimate, but this fix puts the cost on all planning. No planning-time or memory numbers are given. Message #2 already offers a narrower design, which suggests 0001 is not needed for the stated problem.
objections.author_must_show: What planning-time and memory change does 0001 cause on join-heavy queries with no foreign tables, such as a many-way join on indexed local tables?

critic.reasoning: Patch 0001 touches only pathnode.c, and add_path() runs for every rel of every query. The thread gives no planning-time or memory numbers, and message #2 itself calls the narrower design a better fit for the current model.

objections.title: New FDW callback is a permanent API with no shown contract
objections.failure_scenario: An FDW author implements the callback and returns a path whose cost or restrictions do not match the new required_outer. reparameterize_path() trusts it, and the Append is built on wrong costs or wrong quals. Nothing in core checks the result, so the bug shows up as wrong plans or wrong results in the field.
objections.argument: Message #2 adds an FDW callback called from reparameterize_path(), but the material shows no name, signature, documentation, or rules on what the FDW must return or may refuse. Once released, FdwRoutine members are hard to change or remove. Message #3 points to an earlier proposal of the same API from the foreign-table-inheritance work, and no comparison is given. A committer would likely want one agreed contract before adding a member to FdwRoutine.
objections.author_must_show: What are the callback's signature and documented contract, and how does it differ from the earlier FDW API proposal mentioned in message #3?

critic.reasoning: The failure scenario is weak, because core trusts every FDW path callback the same way. The request stands: the material shows no signature or contract, and message #3 asks for a comparison with the earlier API that nobody has answered.

refuted.title: postgres_fdw cost cache has no stated key or lifetime
refuted.failure_scenario: If cached estimates outlive one planning run, a remote table that grows after the cache entry is made keeps its old low cost. The planner keeps choosing a parameterized nested loop that is now slow, and the user cannot tell why EXPLAIN costs disagree with a fresh remote EXPLAIN.
refuted.argument: Patch 0002 in message #2 caches remote EXPLAIN results for parameterized paths. The proposal does not say what the cache key is, where the cache lives, or when entries go away. If the cache is per planning run, this objection goes away. Otherwise postgres_fdw gains an invalidation problem it does not have today.
refuted.author_must_show: What is the cache keyed on, and is it freed at the end of each planning run or does it persist longer?

critic.reasoning: The scenario depends on a cache that outlives one planning run, and the proposal does not say it does. Message #2 describes reuse for paths "already costed and rejected", which points to the same planning run, and the objection concedes it then goes away.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: The alternative design adds a new FDW callback that reparameterize_path() calls.

touch_points.label: planner behaviour change
touch_points.reason: Both designs change which paths survive, so some queries get a parameterized nested loop where they got a hash join.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: A new FDW callback or a changed add_path() dominance rule limits the fix to master.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: A new FDW API member and a cost cache in postgres_fdw stay for good.

touch_points.label: performance on the hot path
touch_points.reason: Patch 0001 from message #1 changes add_path() in pathnode.c, which every query's planning goes through.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Which design do you plan to pursue: the add_path() change from message #1 or the FDW reparameterization callback from message #2?
If the add_path() patch stays, what planning-time and memory change does it cause on a many-way join of indexed local tables with no foreign tables?
What are the callback's signature and documented contract, including when an FDW may decline to reparameterize a path?
How does the callback differ from the FDW API proposed in the foreign-table-inheritance work that message #3 points to?
What is the postgres_fdw cost cache keyed on, and is it freed at the end of each planning run?

committability.owner_note: Etsuro Fujita gave +1 to the callback design in message #3 and says he proposed this FDW API before. The add_path() patch would need someone who knows planner path dominance, and nobody has reviewed it.
committability.liability: The owner signs for a new FDW API member that external FDWs may implement and that is hard to change after release. The owner also signs for plan changes in postgres_fdw queries and for the correctness of the cost cache.
committability.author_follow_up: Two authors from the same company are active: the second posted a new design two weeks after the first message and created the CommitFest entry. Fujita's question in message #3 has no reply yet.

priority.reason: The defect affects partitioned tables with postgres_fdw partitions and use_remote_estimate, but the shown plan is about 600 times slower than the lost one. The callback design keeps the cost on FDW users and has support in message #3. The patches from message #2 were not read, so review cost is an estimate.

provisional_note: The patch prose for the two patches in message #2 is not in the material, so the callback's contract and the cache's key and lifetime could not be checked. Whether the reparameterized path gets correct costs and quals needs the code.

precedents_retrieved.title: postgres_fdw: support parameterized foreign joins
precedents_retrieved.summary: postgres_fdw would build parameterized foreign-join paths, so a join of foreign tables can be pushed to the remote server with a parameter from an outer local relation. The core planner records the required_outer relations it tried during add_paths_to_joinrel(), and postgresGetForeignJoinPaths() builds parameterized paths for them.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch was marked Ready for Committer but depended on the separate "epqpath-for-foreignjoin" patch and was not committed. It then bitrotted and was moved to Waiting for author. The author did not post an update for about six weeks, so Michael Paquier returned it with feedback. No design objection appears in the visible messages.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
One month and a half after, the already-rotten patch has not been
updated, so I am marking it as returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: A hook for path-removal decision on add_path
precedents_retrieved.summary: A hook for path-removal decision on add_path

precedents_retrieved.title: Async execution of postgres_fdw.
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch made postgres_fdw send the remote query asynchronously from ExecInitForeignScan, so several foreign scans could run on remote servers at the same time. It wrapped PGconn in a new PgFdwConn struct so that several scans could share one connection, and it cancelled a pending async query when another scan or modification used that connection.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Starting the remote query in ExecInitNode is against the documented FDW API, which says execution must not start before IterateForeignScan is called. Tom Lane added that ExecInitNode only builds runtime structures: a scan may never be iterated, for example on the inner side of a nestloop with an empty outer relation, and parameter values for a parameterized scan are not yet available. He also asked to drop the connection wrapper layer, which caused most of the code churn and added unchecked malloc failures.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I certainly appreciate that you've put quite a bit of effort into this
but I'm afraid we can't accept it while it's starting to run a query on
the remote side during the ExecInitNode phase.  The query can not start
executing on the remote side until InterateForeignScan is called.

precedents_retrieved.title: Asynchronous execution on postgres-fdw
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch set adds a core pre-execution callback mechanism, so that nodes can register callbacks that run just before the ExecProc phase, and uses it to start postgres_fdw remote queries asynchronously, with one running query per foreign server. It also offers three experimental ways to set the fetch size: duration-based adaptation, a byte-limited FETCH, and a fetch_size foreign table option.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Heikki Linnakangas marked the entry rejected because a more general solution based on parallel workers was in progress and would largely make this patch obsolete, with the option to revisit it later in the release cycle. Earlier he had objected that the pre-execution callback has the same problems as starting execution in ExecInit, and that queries should start in the first IterateForeignScan() call. Robert Haas and Stephen Frost replied that the design questions were still open, and Stephen Frost did not like that the mechanism was specific to FDWs.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I've marked this as rejected in the commitfest, because others are
working on a more general solution with parallel workers.

precedents_retrieved.title: Push down more UPDATEs/DELETEs in postgres_fdw
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch extends postgres_fdw direct modification so that an UPDATE or DELETE that joins foreign tables on the same server is sent to the remote server as one statement, such as `DELETE ... USING`. It also deparses RETURNING lists that refer to columns of the joined relations.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch reached Ready for Committer, but Robert Haas found in review that it no longer applied after recent changes. He also asked for more comments, use of the new RelOptKind macros, and a regression test for the non-pushed path. The patch went to Waiting for author because it had bitrotted, no new version came, and the entry was returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: No updates have showed up since, so returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: postgres_fdw: evaluate placeholdervars on remote server
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets postgres_fdw evaluate PlaceHolderVars on the remote server, so left, right and full joins that contain PHVs can be pushed down. It also changes how whole-row references are deparsed and builds on the deparser support for subqueries from the full-join pushdown work.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author said he was not satisfied with the patch and that it needed more work, and he did not rebase it for the September 2017 CommitFest after reminders. Robert Haas proposed marking patches like this Returned with Feedback when no rebase arrives before the CommitFest starts, and the author agreed and marked it so.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Frankly, I think things where there was a ping multiple weeks before
the CommitFest started and no rebase before it started should be
regarded as untimely submissions, and summarily marked Returned with
Feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: TRUNCATE on foreign tables
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add an optional ExecForeignTruncate callback to FdwRoutine so that TRUNCATE works on foreign tables, including foreign partitions of a partitioned table. The callback gets the foreign tables of one server as a list, with DropBehavior and restart_seqs, and postgres_fdw sends one remote TRUNCATE for them.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier marked it returned with feedback because the implementation, the docs and the tests needed more work. The open issues at that point were ONLY handling, since TRUNCATE ONLY on a local foreign table could truncate the whole inheritance tree on the remote server, and a possible separate truncatable option for postgres_fdw. Missing postgres_fdw documentation and missing inheritance tests were also still open.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: For now, as the patch needs more work for its implementation, docs and tests, I am marking it as returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: postgres_fdw: Handle boolean comparison predicates
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Daniel Gustafsson, Ashutosh Bapat, Ronan Dunklau
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes postgres_fdw push the boolean tests IS [NOT] TRUE/FALSE/UNKNOWN down to the remote server. It deparses each test into an equivalent expression, such as (NOT x OR x IS NULL) for IS NOT TRUE.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch stopped applying to HEAD, and the author did not post a rebased version after Daniel Gustafsson asked for one, so it was returned at the end of the commitfest. Ashutosh Bapat and Ronan Dunklau also asked why the tests are rewritten instead of sent as written, and asked for a test on a boolean column. The author did not answer these points.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: The patch no longer applies to HEAD, can you please submit a rebased version?

precedents_retrieved.title: Reducing memory usage of creating foreign key between partitioned tables
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes RelationBuildPartitionDesc build a partitioned table's partition descriptor in a temporary memory context and delete that context afterwards, so the temporary memory is freed instead of being leaked. The aim was to stop the out-of-memory failures seen when adding a foreign key between two partitioned tables that each have thousands of partitions; later revisions were discussed for back-patching to v12.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected early that leak management belongs at the caller level, not inside RelationBuildPartitionDesc. Amit Langote then noted that commit 5b9312378 had already removed the repeated rebuild that caused the leak in v13, so the remaining question was back-patching. Tom Lane found no visible leak in HEAD and saw that the test case was still impractical because of planner cost in RI_Initial_Check, so he saw no reason to back-patch a leak fix. He recommended rejecting the patch and suggested back-porting 5b9312378 instead if a back-branch fix were wanted.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
In short, I don't see a reason why we need this patch in any branch,
so I recommend rejecting it.

precedents_retrieved.objection:
This is almost a straight revert of commit fff518d, which itself was a
revert of 7d3bf73ac.

It turns out that commit 8aa9dd74, which sorted dependent objects before
deletion in DROP OWNED BY, was not sufficient to make all remaining

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix index-only scan plans, take 2.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Fix index-only scan plans, take 2.
Reverted commit(s): Fix index-only scan plans when not all index columns can be returned.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Commit 4ace45677 failed to fix the problem fully, because the
same issue of attempting to fetch a non-returnable index column
can occur when rechecking the indexqual after using a lossy index
operator.  Moreover, it broke EXPLAIN for such indexquals (which
indicates a gap in our test cases :-().

Revert the code changes of 4ace45677 in favor of adding a new field
to struct IndexOnlyScan, containing a version of the indexqual that
can be executed against the index-returned tuple without using any
non-returnable columns.  (The restrictions imposed by check_index_only
guarantee this is possible, although we may have to recompute indexed
expressions.)  Support construction of that during setrefs.c
processing by marking IndexOnlyScan.indextlist entries as resjunk
if they can't be returned, rather than removing them entirely.
(We could alternatively require setrefs.c to look up the IndexOptInfo
again, but abusing resjunk this way seems like a reasonably safe way
to avoid needing to do that.)

This solution isn't great from an API-stability standpoint: if there
are any extensions out there that build IndexOnlyScan structs directly,
they'll be broken in the next minor releases.  However, only a very
invasive extension would be likely to do such a thing.  There's no
change in the Path representation, so typical planner extensions
shouldn't have a problem.

As before, back-patch to all supported branches.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent records a reason that applies here. P2 and P9 touch add_path() but have no recorded reason, and P1 was returned only because it bitrotted. Message #3 says Fujita proposed a similar FDW reparameterize API during the foreign-table-inheritance work, but the thread does not say why it was not adopted. A committer would likely ask for a comparison with that proposal, but the proposal gives no reason against this design.

From the standards and compatibility angle there is nothing to object to: no SQL syntax, GUC, catalog object, pg_dump or psql change is proposed. Plan changes for existing queries are the intended fix, and an optional FDW callback follows existing FdwRoutine practice. The callback signature and the cache keying and invalidation in postgres_fdw are not shown, so the client-visible effect of cached remote estimates could not be checked.

Both designs only change planner path selection and add an in-memory FDW callback and cost cache. Neither touches on-disk format, WAL, catalogs or the wire protocol. A new FdwRoutine member would limit the alternative to master, which is normal for a new feature, and existing FDWs leave it unset.

The proposal changes path retention in add_path() and adds an FDW callback for reparameterization. Neither touches privileges, catalogs, authentication or user-visible data, so I see no security objection. One point cannot be checked without the code: the postgres_fdw estimate cache should be keyed by user mapping, so a role that switches users with SET ROLE in a session never reuses remote estimates taken under another role's credentials.

Committability: Etsuro Fujita, who knows postgres_fdw, is engaged and supports the reparameterization design. This lowers the maintenance concern for the callback approach. The objections above are about 0001's cost and the unspecified callback and cache contracts.

Postgres has no existing way to get this plan reliably. Settings such as enable_hashjoin = off and hint extensions only force a plan, and a set_rel_pathlist_hook path would still be discarded by add_path(). The alternative design extends reparameterize_path(), which is the existing mechanism, so it adds no second way to do the same job.

Message #1 shows a real plan-quality defect: a hash join of about 1739 ms is chosen over a parameterized nested loop of about 2.7 ms. The cause is a lost parameterized path, not cost. The trigger is common in postgres_fdw sharding, where an empty or near-empty partition sits next to large ones under use_remote_estimate. The interest has lasted: in message #3, Fujita supports the reparameterization approach and says he proposed the same FDW API years ago. Costs mostly fall on FDW users, except that patch 0001 changes add_path() for every query, which is a design question for other angles. One demand gap is small: the optional postgres_fdw cache comes with no numbers showing that repeated remote EXPLAIN calls cost real planning time. That gap does not justify a rejection.
